name: MusiQL
summary: A full-stack music app where a playlist is a saved query instead of a fixed list.
description: MQL is a small query language I designed for the job: it parses to an AST, gets checked against a whitelisted schema, and compiles down to parameterized SQL — so a playlist stays a live question about the catalog rather than a snapshot of it. A catalog ETL rebuilds millions of rows with no downtime, and Spotify OAuth exports any playlist straight to a user's own account.

name: Plannit
summary: A self-hosted personal finance app, so the numbers never leave a machine you control.
description: Every query is owner-scoped at the data-access layer, bank-statement imports are duplicate-safe on re-upload, and a projection engine models retirement against real balances. 230+ automated tests back it, and CodeQL is at zero alerts because the XSS, ReDoS, and path-traversal findings were fixed rather than suppressed.

name: Heardit
summary: Letterboxd for music — rate what you listen to, follow people, and keep a listen-later queue.
description: Ratings, follows, and a queue over a PostgreSQL catalog. The social feed is the interesting part: its queries are batched to avoid the N+1 reads that make this kind of app fall over the moment someone follows more than a handful of people.

name: Personal Site
summary: This site — a React and TypeScript static site, built and published straight from GitHub.
description: Frosted-glass surfaces over an ambient gradient, with light and dark handled as a single token override so the two themes cannot drift apart. Every word on the site is structured JSON checked into the repo and type-checked at build time, and the text contrast was measured against WCAG rather than eyeballed. GitHub Actions builds it and publishes to Pages.
